newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Modenas seen cutting year losses.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Modenas seen cutting year losses.

text.p: Motorsikal dan Enjin Nasional Bhd (Modenas) is confident of reducing its accumulated losses in the year ending March 31, 1997, DRB-Hicom group managing director Mohamed Saleh Sulong said on Monday.

Amid a strong response to the national motorcycle produced by Modenas, the company was confident of cutting its accumulated losses to 4.7 million ringgit for the year from an earlier-projected 27.5 million ringgit, the national Bernama news agency quoted him as saying.
Since its launching on November 16, 1996, the 110 c.c. "Kriss" has received orders totalling 20,000 units, of which half have been delivered to dealers, he said.

To meet the demand, Modenas' production capacity at its plant in the northern Kedah state, would be expanded to 100,000 units per year. Modenas had projected in October that it would triple annual production capacity to 350,000 in three years.

Modenas is a 600 million ringgit joint venture between two Malaysian companies and two Japanese partners. Malaysian automotive group Diversified Resources Bhd (DRB) holds a 55 percent stake in the company and the federal investment agency Khazanah Nasional a 15 percent interest.
Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd holds a 19 percent stake and Nissho Iwai the remaining 11 percent.
